extracted.intended_audience: researchers and advanced students of humour research, linguistics, and cognitive science
extracted.subtask_description: Analytic framework and methods for studying verbal humour: how to analyze jokes, the linguistic devices that produce humour (puns, misinterpretation, incongruity-resolution), and computational/pragmatic approaches to modelling them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assumptions and methodology for rigorous study
rubrics_metrics.description: The author begins by considering how to study jokes rigorously: the assumptions to make, the guidelines to follow and the pitfalls to avoid.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes critique of other work on humour, introduces key concepts, and demonstrates the lack of agreement about what a theory of humour should look like; intended to guide researchers on methodological choices when analyzing jokes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Analyze humorous items in precise detail
rubrics_metrics.description: Analyze humorous items in precise detail, in order to understand their mechanisms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Presented as a central step toward building a theory of humour; detailed micro-analysis of individual jokes is used to reveal operative mechanisms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Language devices used in jokes (puns, misinterpretation, etc.)
rubrics_metrics.description: The language devices used in various jokes, such as puns or humour based on misinterpretation, are analysed in detail.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasises identifying and characterising specific linguistic devices that generate humour; links to chapters on structure of puns and manipulation of interpretations for examples and analyses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Incongruity and its resolution
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treats incongruity-resolution as a central mechanism in verbal humour; analyses how unexpected or conflicting interpretations are created and then resolved to produce comedy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Models of incongruity-resolution
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Presents and compares concrete models explaining how incongruity and its resolution operate in jokes, useful for evaluating which model best accounts for a given joke's workings.

rubrics_metrics.name: General theory of verbal humour
rubrics_metrics.description: The General Theory of Verbal Humour.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Develops and demonstrates proposals for how best to analyze the workings of simple jokes and offers general suggestions about language devices central to joke construction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Joke similarity and identity
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Addresses criteria for determining when two jokes are similar or identical; useful for classification, corpus analysis, and tracking variants/memes of jokes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manipulating interpretations to create humour
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers techniques by which speakers/writers guide audience interpretations (ambiguity, priming, context shifts) to produce humorous effects; relevant both to analysis and to joke construction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Structure of puns
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Detailed analysis of the components and mechanisms that make puns work (lexical ambiguity, phonological similarity, sense-switching); informs both evaluation of pun quality and methods for constructing puns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Computational studies of humour
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examines computational approaches and models for representing, detecting, or generating verbal humour; provides methods and case studies for computational evaluation and modelling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pragmatic and discourse issues in joke interpretation
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Considers context, conversational implicature, and discourse-level factors that affect joke comprehension and effectiveness; highlights pragmatic constraints on how jokes function.

rubrics_metrics.name: Speculations on higher-level joke structure
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Offers hypotheses and higher-level theorising about the architecture of jokes beyond specific devices; useful as heuristics for researchers seeking broad explanatory accounts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Future directions for humour research
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Suggests areas for further research and development in the linguistic and computational study of humour; frames open problems and potential methodological advances.
